summary: Refactor Base and Head runtime responsibilities into explicit rule, targeting and combat boundaries without changing gameplay, persistence keys, registry identities or network payload schemas.

authoritative_state: TurretBaseBlockEntity remains the owner of mutable inventory, energy, trust and persistence state.
TurretHeadBlockEntity remains the owner of cooldown, target presentation and aim persistence state.
Targeting and combat services receive immutable inputs and execute only on the server thread.

fields: Base save/load keys remain unchanged, including legacy active/mode reads.
Head cooldown, aim and priority keys remain unchanged.
Real old-save load and save/load round-trip are required after each split stage.

flows.purpose: Preserve existing per-shot turret aim visual updates.
validation: Payload type and field order stay unchanged.
Only bounded presentation state is sent to clients.

client_boundary.dedicated_server_fallback: All services run on common/server classes and never load client-only classes.

budgets.scope: 100 turret bases, 100 turret heads and 100 fixed targets after 200 tick warmup
budgets.measurement: The fixture's 200 server-thread tick intervals are recorded with System.nanoTime; candidate p95 may increase no more than 10 percent over same-machine baseline, with an absolute 0.25 ms floor when baseline p95 is below 1 ms. JFR ServerTickTime and ExecutionSample remain required independent evidence.

hot_paths: TurretBaseBlockEntity server tick and attachment views
performance.measurement_environment: Fixed Windows host, Java 21, NeoForge 21.1.234, identical JVM/config/workspace protocol, three baseline and three candidate runs.

mods.fallback: The mod refuses to load outside the pinned NeoForge 21.1 line.

criteria.statement: Existing gameplay behavior, registry IDs, payload schemas and client/server boundaries remain unchanged.
criteria.observation: Existing behavior GameTests, static gate and dedicated-server smoke pass after the refactor.

criteria.statement: Base, Head and Projectile persistence keys remain readable and round-trip without loss.
criteria.observation: Key ledger, new-object round-trip and real old-save load/save/reload all pass.

criteria.statement: Target selection and combat execution have explicit service boundaries that do not call back into Head.
criteria.observation: Services accept bounded inputs, Head owns orchestration state, and static inspection finds no Head-to-service-to-Head cycle.

criteria.statement: The fixed 100/100 pressure scenario does not regress server tick p95 beyond the declared budget.
criteria.observation: Three baseline and three candidate fixture/JFR runs complete and the generated report passes the p95 threshold with independent JFR evidence.

steps: Run one client session after automation is complete.
Check GUI energy/configuration, Jade, Shift tooltip, Beam and projectile visuals.
Change dimension/world, disconnect to menu, reconnect, run F3+T, then exit normally.
manual_checks.expected: All existing client behavior remains unchanged and no client-only state leaks across world or connection boundaries.

non_goals: Changing turret balance, configuration defaults, registry IDs, save keys or network payload fields.
Splitting TurretProjectileEntity movement or tracking without profiler evidence.
Changing or iterating the external .agents toolkit.
Replacing the final manual client acceptance with AI or a server-only test.
